coarse_labels.person: any identifiable single individual, including deities and anthropomorphic mythological figures
coarse_labels.place: a politically, culturally, or geographically defined location, including fictional spaces and structures like temples, buildings, specific urban areas (e.g., gymnasia), and houses
coarse_labels.collective: a named group of people or other creatures with shared identifiable characteristics on social, intellectual, political, national, family, mythical, or ethnic basis
coarse_labels.creature: mythical or real precisely identifiable non-human, non-anthropomorphic creatures
coarse_labels.event: significant named events identified by a string with a precise boundary
coarse_labels.language: languages and dialects clearly identified as such
coarse_labels.object: artifacts or groups of artifacts clearly identified with a name, such as ships, weapons, statues, columns, dedications, etc
coarse_labels.time: any absolute date or time expression
coarse_labels.work: titles of literary or non-literary works, in any form
coarse_labels.miscellaneous: entities that do not (yet) have a specific first-level tag among those provided

fine_labels.person:
name: default when no finer classification applies or is possible. The most usual.
author: A person clearly mentioned in relation to works they have authored. This tag may be modified or even omitted for project-specific goals.
ancestry: A designation or expression that refers unambiguously to one individual by using a family name, patronymic, matronymic, or other indication of lineage or familial relationships.
epithet: A capitalized epithet used to refer unambiguously to one individual, including nicknames, titles, and other appellatives.
ethnic: An ethnonym, demonym, or other word used to identify persons by means of their membership to a geographically or ethnically defined group. This tag is exclusively used with persons or collectives, as ethnics are mainly used in the ancient world to identify individuals via ethnic memberships.
derivative: An adjective derived from a personal name, used to identify things that are not individuals or collectives. Only the derivative is annotated, as the common noun in the expression does not act as a rigid designator.
fine_labels.place:
name: default when no finer classification applies or is possible. The most usual.
astronomy: Named stars, constellations, and planets.
epithet: A capitalized epithet used to refer unambiguously to one location, including nicknames, titles, and other appellatives.
derivative: An adjective derived from a toponym, used to identify things that are not locations or collectives. Only the derivative is annotated, as the common noun in the expression does not act as a rigid designator.
fine_labels.collective:
name: default when no finer classification applies or is possible. The most usual.
ancestry: A designation or expression that refers unambiguously to one group of individuals by using a family name, patronymic, matronymic, or other indication of lineage or familial relationships.
animal: A collective of creatures clearly identifiable with an animal species.
astronomy: Named groups of stars, constellations, and planets.
ethnic: An ethnonym, demonym, or other word used to identify collectives by means of their membership to a geographically or ethnically defined group. This tag is exclusively used with collectives, as ethnics are mainly used in the ancient world to identify individuals via ethnic memberships.
organization: A collective that is an organization (e.g., a military unit).
epithet: A capitalized epithet used to refer unambiguously to one collective, including nicknames, titles, and other appellatives.
derivative: An adjective derived from a group name used to identify things that are not individuals or collectives. Only the derivative is annotated, as the common noun in the expression does not act as a rigid designator.
fine_labels.creature:
name: default when no finer classification applies or is possible. The most usual.
animal: A creature clearly identifiable with an animal species.
astronomy: Named stars, groups of stars, constellations, and planets.
